newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Council of Europe says Albania local polls fair.
newsitem.headline: Council of Europe says Albania local polls fair.

text.p: The Council of Europe said on Tuesday it was satisfied with Albania's second round of local elections though some irregularities should be examined by the Central Electoral Commission (CEC).

"The Council of Europe observer delegation is generally satisfied with the conduct of the second round of elections on October 27 although it regrets that again there were some instances of irregularities serious enough to warrant careful examination by the CEC," a statement, faxed to Reuters, said.

The ruling Democrats have claimed 90.6 percent of city halls and 86.7 percent of communes in the vote. The Socialists, reformed heirs to the communists, gained just 6.25 percent of city halls and 4.5 percent of communes, down from 51 percent and 59.8 percent respectively in 1992.
Official results were due later in the week.

The Council of Europe -- the continent's human rights watchdog body set up in 1949 -- said the poll represented a step forward for Albanian democracy. Nevertheless it criticised individual failures to implement the electoral law properly and found fault with the presentation of voter lists.
It also cited serious incidents regarding the behaviour of some party representatives.

"(But) apart from these isolated incidents in the districts visited the polling can be said to have been sufficiently free and fair to be accepted as a reliable expression of the inhabitants", it said.
The Socialists insisted that the local ballot was far from free and fair but acknowledged it marked an improvement on parliamentary elections in May and June.
"Small improvements served simply...to create the impression of free and calm elections," the party said in a statement.
